checks.desc: Hostname uses xn-- (punycode) or non-ASCII letters. This is the IDN homograph / homoglyph attack: Cyrillic 'а' looks like Latin 'a' but is a different domain
One domain label mixes scripts (Latin + Cyrillic/Greek). Real brands never do
Map look-alike characters to ASCII (а→a, ο→o, ӏ→l, rn→m, vv→w, 0→o, 1→l) and compare with the brand list
Zero-width characters or right-to-left override inside a URL or domain
Damerau-Levenshtein distance 1-2 from a known brand domain, keyboard-adjacent swaps, dropped or doubled letters
Brand plus a lure word (hdfc-kyc-update, sbi-refund). Your brand_typosquat covers brand keywords; this adds the lure list
Brand appears as a subdomain while the registered domain is something else (sbi.secure-login.xyz)
Brand name in the path of an unrelated domain (evil.xyz/sbi/login)
URL contains user@host so the visible part is not the real host (http://sbi.co.in@evil.xyz)
IP address as host, including decimal, hex and octal forms
Very long URL, many dots, hyphens, digits or subdomains
High-entropy or random-looking label (generated domains), using entropy and vowel ratio
Known shorteners (bit.ly, tinyurl and others) and long redirect chains
Brand-themed page on free hosts (github.io, pages.dev, vercel.app, netlify.app, blogspot, weebly, firebaseapp, forms.gle, telegra.ph, sites.google.com)
Dynamic DNS or tunnel hosts (ngrok, trycloudflare, duckdns, no-ip)
login, verify, kyc, update, secure, claim, refund, reward in host or path
Unusual port in the URL
URL carries a script-injection payload (<script>, onerror=, javascript:, encoded forms). We detect payloads in the link; we never test sites for XSS
SQL-injection or path-traversal strings in the URL (' OR 1=1, ../)
Parameter such as ?url=http://other or ?redirect= pointing off-site, often on a trusted domain
data:, javascript:, intent:// or upi:// links where a web link is expected
Doubly percent-encoded URL to hide content
Plain http for a page that asks for data or payment
.apk, .exe, .scr, .bat or .jar in the URL path (your suspicious_downloads checks page links; this checks the URL itself)
Registered less than 180 days ago, or registration unverifiable
Registrant hidden behind a privacy or proxy service
Cheap, disposable TLDs (.xyz, .top, .sbs, .cfd, .icu)
Domain contains a bank or NBFC brand keyword but is not that brand's real domain
No valid SSL certificate
Domain is on the police-confirmed list or in your own case database
Registered for one year only, or expiring very soon
Certificate issued days ago, free CA only, many brand names in the SAN list, name mismatch (uses your CT feed)
Many A records with a very short TTL
Same IP or nameserver as a confirmed fraud domain in your own database
Registrar or nameserver heavily reused across your fraud cases
Cloud, VPS or anonymising host (indicative only, never proof)
Indian lender hosted abroad (indicative only)
Sender domain with no SPF/DMARC (for email checks)
Predatory wording: no credit check, no documents, no CIBIL
Advance fee, processing fee, guaranteed approval
Pressure wording: act now, limited time
No privacy policy, terms or grievance channel
No email or phone anywhere on the page
Skeleton landing page with very little content
Says it is a mediator or lead-generation site. Decides the category, not scored
India lender page with no RBI, NBFC or Key Fact Statement mention
Names a lender that is not in the local RBI list
Browser lands on a different domain than requested

en: Do not click the link, install the app, call the number or share any OTP / PIN.
If you already paid or shared details: call 1930 now and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Ask your bank to block the card / UPI.
Keep screenshots and the message as evidence. Report the number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu).

2.title: Part time job! Like YouTube videos and earn Rs 3000 daily from home. Join our Telegram group t.me/ea…
2.why: Several strong warning signs that back each other up

en: Do not click the link, install the app, call the number or share any OTP / PIN.
If you already paid or shared details: call 1930 now and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Ask your bank to block the card / UPI.
Keep screenshots and the message as evidence. Report the number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu).

मैसेज और स्क्रीनशॉट सबूत के लिए संभाल कर रखें।
